purpose: Acebutolol is used to treat high blood pressure and certain irregular heart rhythms (arrhythmias). Lowering blood pressure helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney problems. It helps your heart beat more regularly and with less effort.
how_it_works: Your heart has special receptors that respond to stress hormones like adrenaline, which can make your heart beat faster and harder. Acebutolol blocks those receptors in your heart, slowing it down and reducing the force of each beat. This takes pressure off your heart and helps keep your blood pressure and heart rate at a safer, steadier level.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired or sluggish, dizziness, slow heartbeat, cold hands or feet, headache, upset stomach, nausea, and trouble sleeping. Some people may also notice mild shortness of breath with activity.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor — stopping abruptly can trigger chest pain or even a heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have asthma, diabetes, or kidney problems, as this medication can affect those conditions. It can also mask the warning signs of low blood sugar if you are diabetic. Avoid if you have a very slow heart rate or certain types of heart block.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 400 mg once a day or split into two doses (200 mg twice a day). Your doctor may increase it up to 800 mg per day if needed. For heart rhythm problems, dosing is typically 200 mg twice a day, and may be adjusted. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
